IncidentBot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT PAGE: 2135790246 - Elevated 5xxs and request backlog observed for /v1/generate across hosted and dedicated. Paging oncall @Alex (primary). Auto-escalation to @eng-oncall after 2m.
Alex: I'm on pager. looking at console now. can someone drop the slow-query dashboard link?
Sara: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/slow-path - customers reporting timeouts starting ~11:02 UTC
Alex: initial glance: spike in queue depth for hotpath queues, GPUs at ~98% on pool-3. CPU ok. @Mateo can you check runtime traces (kv cache warmup?)
Mateo: pulling logs and traces. seeing many cold-starts for recent model-variant v2-q4 in dedicated pools. KV cache miss rate jumped ~x10 around 11:01.
Priya: HPA didn't scale for pods annotated autoscale.redwood/quick=true. CPU metric stable but queue-length metric high. suspect metrics adapter throttle.
Alex: paste HPA output
Priya: ```kubectl get hpa -n inference hotpath-hpa
NAME         REFERENCE                 TARGETS         MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS   AGE
hotpath-hpa  Deployment/hotpath-svc    5%/80% (qlen)   5         50        5          3h
```
Priya: adapter reports 0q/s for a short window at 11:00:45 due to 503 from metric-server. then it recovered but controller didn't reconcile quickly
Casey: pool-3 metrics:
pool-3: total_gpus=64, used_gpus=63, pending_warmups=22, avg_warmup_ms=2800, free_nodes=0
saturation_pct=98.4%
Alex: queue depth dump (hotpath):
11:00:30 queue_len=1200
11:01:00 queue_len=3100
11:02:00 queue_len=5200
avg_latency_ms=1200 -> 3400
Mateo: trace for a timed-out request:
- req arrive 11:01:07
- assigned to pod A (cold): start model load 11:01:08
- load weights 11:01:08 -> 11:01:11 (3s)
- kv cache populate starts 11:01:11 -> hits delayed due to NFS read 11:01:14
- overall response fail 11:01:20 (timeout)
Priya: hypothesis 1: metric-server transient caused HPA to not scale in time -> pool saturated -> requests queued -> cold starts and warmup backlog.
Priya: hypothesis 2: NFS latency spike causing kv cache warmup to be slow on newly created pods -> cold starts heavier.
Alex: mitigation options: (A) increase hotpath HPA minpods to 20, (B) enable fallback to v1-quant for hosted, (C) throttle non-SLA customers.
Casey: I can bump HPA min to 20 and open reservation on pool-4 for burst.
Mateo: fallback toggle ready at /ops/rollouts/fallback. reduces quality but cuts warmup. need approval for global flip.
Alex: do hosted-only fallback for 30m and monitor. Sara, notify affected customers.
Sara: crafting message now. tagging billing for enterprise accounts.
Priya: running HPA patch:
kubectl patch hpa hotpath-hpa -n inference -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":20}}'
Casey: reserving 8 gpus on pool-4. reservation-id: r-4832. scheduling should relieve queue in ~60-90s.
IncidentBot: :white_check_mark: Mitigations recorded: HPA min=20, pool-4 reservation r-4832, hosted fallback enabled 30m.
Mateo: enabling fallback -> flipped to v1-quant for hosted. rolling 400 pods.
Alex: monitoring latency and errors. @Priya capture timeline for RCA doc. include logs here.
Priya: timeline snippet:
11:00:35 - first elevated 5xx spike on /v1/generate
11:00:45 - metric-server 503s observed
11:01:00 - queue depth rising >3k
11:01:30 - pool-3 saturation ~98%
11:02:10 - customer timeouts start
11:03:00 - HPA min bumped to 20
11:03:10 - pool-4 reservation requested
11:04:00 - hosted fallback flip
11:06:30 - queue depth trending down
11:10:00 - error rates near baseline
Sara: customers updated in #customers-ops. follow-up RCA ETA 24h.
Priya: next RCA actions: (1) investigate metric-server 503s and adapter retries, (2) check NFS latency 10:55-11:05, (3) evaluate HPA reconciliation latency for queue-based scale, (4) consider pre-warm policy for dedicated pools.
Alex: assigning owners: metric-server adapter: Casey; NFS latency: Mateo; HPA controller + alerts: Priya; customer comms: Sara
Casey: opening INFRA ticket for metric-server fail. note: control-plane GC spike at 10:59 might be related.
Mateo: collecting NFS iostat and mount logs. checking kernel updates on pool-3 nodes.
Priya: will run synthetic load replay to reproduce HPA lag and add alert for pending_warmups > 10.
Alex: handing off in 20m. Priya primary. creating RCA doc link: https://docs.redwood.ai/rca/autoscale-2135790246
Priya: snapshotting logs to s3://incidents/2135790246/ retention 90d
Casey: created ticket INFRA-8923 and reservation audit rsv-4832
Mateo: will include trace/span IDs in RCA.
Sara: will follow up with customers once RCA posted.
Alex: thanks team. closing incident channel in 30m unless regressions.
